title: Landmarks of Eko
blurb: Ten places every Lagosian has heard of.

qs.q: Which Catholic cathedral, on the edge of the Brazilian Quarter on Lagos Island, has been the seat of the Archdiocese of Lagos since 1950?
qs.hint: Its French Gothic building was finished in 1939.

qs.q: On Gberefu Island near Badagry, which spot marked the last steps of enslaved people on African soil?
qs.t: Point of No Return, Gberefu (approximate pin)
qs.hint: Its name says there was no coming back.

qs.q: Which palace, first built in 1670 for Oba Gabaro, is the official home of the Oba of Lagos?
qs.hint: Its name means roughly “palace on a pepper farm”.

qs.q: Which 25-storey tower was the British government’s gift for Nigeria’s independence?
qs.hint: It stands west of Tafawa Balewa Square and was later called Defence House.

qs.q: Which theatre in Iganmu was finished in 1976 for FESTAC ’77?
qs.hint: In 2025 it was renamed after a Nobel laureate.

qs.q: In which stadium did 85,000 people watch Nigeria beat Algeria 3–0 in the 1980 Nations Cup final?
qs.hint: It opened in 1972 in Surulere.

qs.q: Which new district is being built on sand dredged from the sea in front of Bar Beach?
qs.hint: Its sea wall is nicknamed the Great Wall of Lagos.

qs.q: Which venue in Ikeja is home to the yearly Felabration festival?
qs.hint: It is run by Femi and Yeni Kuti.

qs.q: Which fishing community stands on stilts over the Lagos Lagoon, near the Third Mainland Bridge?
qs.hint: It is often called the “Venice of Africa”.

qs.q: Which Anglican cathedral on the Marina was completed in 1946?
qs.hint: Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther’s relics were moved here in 1976.

qs.q: Nigeria’s first storey building was built by missionaries in 1842–1845. In which town does it stand?
qs.hint: The same coastal town as the Point of No Return.

qs.q: Which Afro-Brazilian mosque on Martins Street was opened in 1894?
qs.hint: It is named after the businessman who paid for it.

qs.q: Which square is the heart of Popo Aguda, the Brazilian Quarter?
qs.hint: It carries a Portuguese family name.

qs.q: Which memorial park now stands on the site of the old Broad Street Prison?
qs.hint: It opened for the 50th anniversary of independence.

qs.q: Fela rebuilt his home in Ikeja after soldiers burned the first one in 1977. What is it called today?
qs.hint: He named his compound a “republic”.

qs.q: Which Badagry museum is the former barracoon of a 19th-century chief?
qs.hint: The chief’s first name was Seriki.

qs.q: Which railway terminus is the southern end of the Lagos–Ibadan line opened in 1901?
qs.hint: It is on an island between Lagos Island and Ebute Metta.

qs.q: Nigeria’s first deep sea port was inaugurated on 22 January 2023. What is it called?
qs.hint: It sits in the Lagos Free Zone in Ibeju-Lekki.

qs.q: Which refinery, designed for 650,000 barrels a day, was commissioned in May 2023?
qs.hint: It carries the name of Africa’s richest man.

qs.q: Which nature reserve in Lekki has a canopy walkway about 400 m long?
qs.hint: It was founded by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation in 1990.
